title: Introduction to JavaScript
html:
The language of the web — a dynamic, garbage-collected, single-threaded language with first-class functions, now running everywhere from browsers to servers to phones.

JavaScript — a high-level, dynamically typed, multi-paradigm language (procedural, object-oriented via prototypes, functional). Its official specification is ECMAScript (ECMA-262); a new edition ships every June.

Why JavaScript?

The only language browsers run natively

HTML gives structure, CSS gives style, JavaScript gives behaviour. (WebAssembly runs alongside it, but JS is the glue.)

Runs everywhere

Servers (Node.js, Deno, Bun), mobile (React Native), desktop (Electron), edge functions, databases (MongoDB shell).

First-class functions

Functions are values: pass them, return them, store them. Closures make callbacks and modules natural.

Asynchronous by design

A single thread plus an event loop handles thousands of concurrent I/O operations without blocking.

A short history

YearMilestone
1995Brendan Eich writes it in ~10 days at Netscape (Mocha → LiveScript → JavaScript).
1997Standardised as ECMAScript 1 by Ecma International.
2009ES5: strict mode, JSON, Array.prototype.map/filter/reduce. Node.js is released.
2015ES6 / ES2015 — the big one: let/const, arrows, classes, modules, promises, destructuring, Map/Set.
2016 →Yearly editions: async/await (2017), ?. and ?? (2020), top-level await (2022), toSorted (2023), Object.groupBy (2024)…
Name

JavaScript has nothing to do with Java — the name was a 1995 marketing decision. ECMAScript is the spec; JavaScript is the most famous implementation of it.

Engines and runtimes

An engine parses and executes JavaScript. A runtime wraps an engine and adds APIs to talk to the outside world (DOM, files, network, timers).

EngineUsed by
V8 (C++)Chrome, Edge, Node.js, Deno, Electron
SpiderMonkeyFirefox (the first JS engine ever)
JavaScriptCoreSafari, Bun, React Native (with Hermes as an alternative)
RuntimeExtra APIs it provides
Browserwindow, document (DOM), fetch, localStorage, setTimeout, events
Node.jsfs, path, process, http, Buffer, EventEmitter, CommonJS + ESM modules
Deno / BunNode-compatible APIs, built-in TypeScript, secure-by-default (Deno)
Watch out

setTimeout, console and fetch are not part of the language — they come from the runtime. The ECMAScript spec itself has no I/O at all.

Your first program

In a browser, open DevTools (F12) → Console and type expressions directly, or load a file with <script src="app.js" defer></script>.

About the examples

All examples in these notes run on Node 24 as an ES module (main.mjs) and show their real output. ES modules are always in strict mode — this matters for this and a few other rules, and is pointed out where relevant.
